title: Sebastiano Foscarini, Venetian ambassador in France, to the Doge, Paris 11 September 1680, despatch no. 117 (ASVe Busta 30 f. 4, DECODE R1871)

steps.what: Fetched R1871-R1873 images with the DECODE cookie and viewed them; identified Foscarini (Paris 11 Sep 1680, despatch no. 117) from the signature and docket.
Followed Tomokiyo's R1872 note to Bonavoglia's page (live site HTTP 500); the Wayback copy lists the Foscarini 1680-09-11 despatch as deciphered but shows only the default (Mocenigo) decipherment.
Transcribed R1871's cipher page (23 lines, 1,839 digits) from deskewed strips with two agents.
Tested pair and self-delimiting ([1-4]*[5-0], [1-5]*[6-0]) segmentations; homophonic annealing gave no Italian.
Found rare digits 0/7/8/9 fixed mod 3 within lines: 3-digit groups; DP segmentation to 612 groups, 211 distinct.
Monotone (ordered syllabary) annealer, 12 seeds, clean Italian 4-gram; synthetic ordered control recovered in part, real text not.
Sukhotin vowel test: vowel-like and consonant-like codes interleave, so the table is not alphabetical.
Free letter-per-code and letter/syllable annealers, 14 seeds: seed-dependent overfit gibberish.
Searched for the key and Bonavoglia's Foscarini page: DECODE Venetian keys R1788-R1790 (16th c., no match); crittologia storia page 404/refused, not archived.

Split from the former combined target r1871 (catalogue 264) under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R1873 (Mocenigo 1558, read from Bonavoglia's decipherment) moved to its own entry r1873; this entry keeps R1871 only, whose outcome is not solved. Earlier steps are kept as recorded.

Brice Dudout (email of 27 Oct 2026) reported Bonavoglia's Foscarini page back online. Retrieved it (r1871_bonavoglia.txt): the full decipherment, 262 words, of the P.S. on rumoured Spanish reinforcements in the Milanese and Louis XIV's plan to raise the Pinerolo garrison to 6,000 men; a few words open in his text ('[Francesi?]269?', '114?', '202.106.100'). His ciphertext viewer still returns HTTP 500, so the decipherment was not aligned with this project's 612-group transcription. Dudout also reports rebuilding the table (a syllabary in blocks of five consecutive codes, blocks out of order; 94.9% agreement with Bonavoglia's text on held-out lines) and points to transcription doubts at L18-19 and L22.

outcome.method_basis: The text is Paolo Bonavoglia's published decipherment (crittologia.eu), retrieved 27 Oct 2026 once his page was back online; nothing was deciphered here, the key was not rebuilt and his text was not aligned with this project's transcription. The project's own ciphertext-only attempt (22 Sept 2026) failed.
outcome.notes: Already deciphered by Bonavoglia; his page was offline during the attempt. Dudout's table (blocks of five codes, out of order) explains why the monotone-syllabary solver failed.

texts.label: R1871, Sebastiano Foscarini, Paris, 11 September 1680, despatch no. 117 (this project's transcription; Paolo Bonavoglia's decipherment)
texts.summary: A postscript Foscarini added after signing his despatch: reports of Spanish reinforcements in the Milanese, and Louis XIV's reported plan to raise the Pinerolo garrison to 6,000 men and spread 16,000 over Dauphiné and Provence, with the Duke of Mantua's illness and a feared Spanish move on Casale; munitions reaching Pinerolo by way of Savoy. Read by Paolo Bonavoglia (crittologia.eu).

reading_review.note: Read Bonavoglia's decipherment as sentences and translated it (texts/R1871_en.md): five coherent paragraphs of 1680 Italian on Spanish troops in the Milanese and the Pinerolo garrison, consistent with the date and the clear signature. The shape check scores 65% of sentences clean because of period spelling with u for v and single consonants (auiso, hauere, trupe, acrescono, dificile), not breaks in sense. His three open number groups are left as he gives them. Not aligned with the cipher groups here.

prior.where: Paolo Bonavoglia, crittologia.eu/storia/SebFoscarini_Parigi16800911.html: full decipherment of the despatch (original ASVe Senato, Dispacci Francia, filza 171A; chancery decipherment in filza 166). Listed before the attempt but offline from Sept 2026; back online and retrieved 27 Oct 2026 on Brice Dudout's pointer.
